title: Matching manuscript word lengths to archived texts
question: Do these available texts contain the manuscript’s sequence of word lengths?
reader_question: Do any of these texts match the manuscript’s word lengths?
summary: No complete pattern matched in 84 eligible texts from 94 available files. The unchanged source scan compared a 2,928-word pattern and two fixed prefixes; it did not replay the historical 224-text corpus.
finding: The best full-pattern counts were 593/2,928 exact, 1,445/2,928 within one rune and 664/2,928 with directional F-count tolerance. The first 400 and 120 word prefixes reached 109/400 and 47/120. These are compatible length positions at an alignment, not decoded words or consecutive matching passages. No complete real pattern matched.
reader_finding: None of the tested alignments matched the complete pattern. The best exact-length alignment agreed at 593 of 2,928 word positions.
limitations: The source admitted 84 of 94 available files and omitted ten texts shorter than 2,928 words, even for the prefix patterns. Only the first 400 and 120 words were tested as shorter windows. Four full-pattern shuffles and two per prefix do not establish a calibrated global probability or statistical equivalence. The source T0 supplied two plant texts and one shuffled control; the preregistered null z gate and degradation floor are not established. This is not the historical 224-text replay or a plaintext/language exclusion.
reader_limit: Only 84 of 94 available texts passed the unchanged length gate. This is not the historical 224-text corpus, and length matches are not decoded words.
next_steps: The linked short-text follow-up checks the ten omitted files where they are long enough for each fixed prefix. Historical missing corpus bytes, other manuscript passages and robustness to changed editions and word boundaries remain unresolved.

scope.representation: Exact pinned Dukotah source manuscript parser and available corpus normalization. First 55 percent-separated segments, 2,928 words; split on dash/period, ignore slash line wraps. The 94 available text files contain 9,808,699 normalized words; 84 files contain 9,799,472 words and meet the unchanged 2,928-word minimum.
scope.procedure: Run unchanged Round 10 L4 source T0 first, then frozen T1: exact length, symmetric slack-one and directional F-count interval. Preserve default blocked FFT, shuffled patterns, raw floating maxima and tie behavior. Independently control all three matchers and recount every saved global winning alignment.
scope.parameters: T1: three full real patterns plus four full permutations with three matchers; first 400 and 120 word interval prefixes with two permutations each; 21 patterns total. Unique alignments per full/400/120 pattern: 9,553,604 / 9,765,956 / 9,789,476. T0: two eligible plant texts, four planted matcher cases and two shuffled matcher cases. No extra corpus globs.
scope.exclusions: Not the historical 224-text / 22,643,594-word replay. Ten available texts shorter than 2,928 are omitted even for shorter patterns. No all-subwindow scan, changed normalization, reordered/noncontiguous plaintext, degradation-floor bound, calibrated global probability, language exclusion or plaintext recovery.

reproduction.environment: Full replay: Python 3.12, NumPy 2.5.4 and the exact external 94-text corpus plus manuscript, prepared as c01-inputs. Output directories must be fresh. PORTABILITY.md gives commands from the extracted bundle root for local Git setup, verification, T0, T1 and comparison with immutable expected outputs. Corpus texts and derived arrays are not bundled. check.py --check is a separate standard-library saved-evidence audit, not the main replay.
